question: Drugs causing hypokalemia are : a) Amphotericin B b) Insulin c) Cyclosporine d) Carbenoxolone e) NSAIDs
analysis: Drugs that can cause hypokalemia include Amphotericin B, which increases renal potassium excretion; Insulin, which promotes cellular uptake of potassium; and Carbenoxolone, which enhances the action of mineralocorticoids leading to potassium loss. Cyclosporine and NSAIDs typically do not cause hypokalemia; in fact, NSAIDs are more commonly associated with hyperkalemia.
